steps: There are four blocks of elements in the periodic table: s-block, p-block, d-block and f-block.
These blocks are helpful because elements in the same block have their last electron entering the same type of subshell.
The blocks help us study and compare the properties of elements.
items.finalAnswer: There are four blocks—s, p, d and f—and they help us study the properties of elements.

steps: Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right in a period.
As we move across a period, the nuclear charge increases while the added electrons enter the same principal shell.
The increased attraction between the nucleus and the electrons pulls the electron cloud closer to the nucleus.
items.finalAnswer: Atomic radius generally decreases across a period because increasing nuclear charge pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus.

steps: Ionization energy generally increases from left to right in a period.
Across a period, nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases.
The outermost electrons are attracted more strongly by the nucleus, so more energy is required to remove an electron.
items.finalAnswer: Ionization energy generally increases across a period because the outermost electrons are held more strongly by the nucleus.

steps: Electronegativity and ionization energy help us predict the type of bond an element will form.
A large difference in electronegativity between two atoms generally favours ionic bond formation; a small difference generally favours covalent bond formation.
items.finalAnswer: Electronegativity, especially the difference between the atoms, and ionization energy help predict the type of bond formed.

steps: Four non-metals that are solids at normal temperature are carbon, sulphur, phosphorus and iodine.
items.finalAnswer: Carbon, sulphur, phosphorus and iodine are solid non-metals at normal temperature.

steps: The second and third periods each contain eight elements because the s and p subshells of their outermost shells are filled.
The first period contains two elements because its first shell has only an s subshell.
The fourth and fifth periods contain eighteen elements because the s, p and d subshells are filled.
The sixth period contains thirty-two elements because the s, p, d and f subshells are filled.
items.finalAnswer: The second and third periods each have eight elements because only their s and p subshells are filled; other periods have different numbers because additional subshells are filled.

steps: The periodic table arranges elements systematically according to their atomic numbers and recurring properties.
Elements with similar properties are placed in the same groups, making their properties easier to compare.
The table helps us study the properties of elements and understand how these properties vary periodically.
It also helps us predict the properties of elements and their compounds.
items.finalAnswer: The periodic table organizes elements by recurring properties, making them easier to study, compare and predict.

steps: Lithium and beryllium have very small atomic sizes compared with the other elements in their respective groups.
Their small size gives them high charge density, high ionization energy and strong polarizing power.
These properties make lithium and beryllium behave differently from the other alkali and alkaline earth metals, respectively.
items.finalAnswer: Lithium and beryllium differ from the other metals in their groups mainly because of their very small atomic size and high charge density.
